trophies.guide: This is the platinum, and it asks for everything else on the list: all 54 other trophies, from the opening mission to 100% completion. There is nothing extra to do beyond the rest of this guide, so treat it as a progress marker rather than a task. Work through the roadmap stages in order and keep an eye on the long grinds — stunts, challenges and collectibles — so they never become a wall at the end. When the last bronze, silver or gold pops, this one follows automatically.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Simply finish Gone Fishing, the opening mission of the story. It introduces the controls and the first characters, and it cannot be skipped or failed permanently — if a section goes wrong you restart at a checkpoint. Play it through to the end cutscene and the trophy pops as the next part of the game opens up. No preparation, collectibles or side content are needed for this one.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1 and the trophy unlocks at the chapter's closing cutscene. Story progress is linear here, so just follow the mission markers and let the game teach you its systems as it goes. If you wander off into side activities, the chapter simply waits for you — nothing in it can be missed. This is also a good moment to start the habit of manual saving before big story beats.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 2 in full and the trophy is yours at the chapter finale. The missions grow longer in this chapter, so keep a stocked inventory of snacks, armour and ammo before starting each one. Nothing here is missable: the chapter only advances when you choose to start its missions, and failed sections restart from checkpoints. If a firefight keeps ending badly, dropping the difficulty for that mission does not affect the trophy.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3 to unlock this trophy. By now the map and most activity types are open, which makes it tempting to drift — the chapter itself stays put until you return to its markers. Keep progressing the marked story missions and the trophy pops at the chapter's final cutscene. Because later collectible and activity grinds are easier with the full map unlocked, pushing through this chapter early pays off.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 4 and the trophy unlocks as the chapter closes. Expect the story's difficulty to step up here, so upgrade your favourite weapons and keep a fast, durable car garaged before starting the late missions. As with every chapter trophy, there is no missable element: missions wait for you and can be replayed from the pause menu afterwards. The trophy pops on completion regardless of mission scores or medals.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Finish the final story mission and this gold trophy is yours. Before starting it, stock up fully — max armour, ammo for your best weapons, and snacks — because finales in this series run long with limited shopping chances. Whatever choices the ending presents, completing the mission is what the trophy checks, so play the ending you prefer. Afterwards the open world remains fully available for the 100% mop-up, so nothing else needs to be done first.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. It appears as a marked main mission during the campaign, and finishing it — cutscenes included — is all the trophy asks. If you are replaying it later, mission replay is available from the pause menu, and a replayed completion still counts. Bring a reliable vehicle and standard weapons; there are no optional objectives tied to the trophy.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions reward a minute of preparation: full armour, a getaway-capable car and your strongest weapons make the escape section far calmer. Follow the mission objectives to the final cutscene and the trophy unlocks, whatever approach you picked inside the heist. A failed attempt simply restarts at a checkpoint, and the mission can also be replayed from the pause menu later.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play when it appears on the map. The trophy only checks completion, so take the mission at your own pace and use checkpoints freely if a section trips you up. It is a main-campaign beat and cannot be skipped past or locked out by side content. If you missed the pop during a first run, replaying the mission from the pause menu also grants it.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. Start it from its map marker when it becomes available in the campaign and play through to the closing cutscene. There are no side objectives or performance thresholds attached to this trophy — finishing is enough. Keep standard supplies topped up beforehand, and remember the mission stays replayable from the pause menu if you ever want to revisit it.
trophies.name: DWNFALL
Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set around Vice City International Airport. Airport missions tend to mix driving, shooting and a timed escape, so arrive with full armour and a fast car parked sensibly. Play the objectives through to the final cutscene and the trophy pops on completion. It cannot be missed permanently, and the pause-menu mission replay covers you if you want a second run.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The name promises a set-piece, so prepare like it is one: best weapons upgraded, armour full, and a stocked snack wheel. Work through the objectives and checkpoints until the mission-complete banner appears and the trophy unlocks with it. As a main mission it is never locked out, and it can be replayed later from the pause menu.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% on the in-game completion tracker. That means the full story plus the required share of stranger strands, activities, challenges, collectibles and exploration tracked elsewhere in this list — use the game's own checklist to see exactly what remains. The efficient route is the roadmap order: story first, then strands, activities and collectibles, checking the percentage after each stage. This gold is usually the last trophy before the platinum, so when it pops, check what is left — it will be very little.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts — the marked stunt jumps and stunt events scattered across Leonida. Each unique stunt counts once it is landed cleanly, so work region by region and use a fast bike or light sports car that is easy to correct in the air. Failed attempts cost nothing but time; you can retry any stunt immediately. Spread this grind across your whole playthrough instead of saving all 250 for the end, and it stops feeling like a grind at all.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of activity in the game once — there are nine types to sample, from races and fishing to the shooting range and arcade games. You do not need to win or even finish most of them; starting each type and taking part is what registers. The natural way is to try each icon the first time you pass one, rather than hunting the list down later. Check your stats or activity log if you lose track of which types you have already touched.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in every Shooting Range challenge — 42 challenges in total across the ranges. Learn one weapon category at a time: gold scores reward accuracy streaks far more than raw speed, so slow down, chain hits, and restart the moment a streak dies early. Challenges stay repeatable forever, and medals are kept per challenge, so chip away at a few golds per session. If one challenge resists, move on and return with fresh aim rather than tilting on it for an hour.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every location — 14 locations in all. Drone races are checkpoint time trials, so the winning skill is a smooth racing line: cut corners early, feather the turns, and learn each course with one slow scouting run before chasing the win. A loss costs nothing and the race restarts instantly, so iterate aggressively on the one or two corners where you bleed time. Do these whenever you pass a new location and the set completes itself.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different is the key word, so repeating one easy race twenty times does not count. Work through the race icons on the map one by one, bringing a car suited to each class and using the first lap to learn the corners. Rubber-banding in story-mode races is forgiving: a clean, crash-free run usually beats a fast, messy one. Wins are tracked permanently, so this builds steadily alongside normal exploration.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal, the fishing character, in one of his fishing challenges. Find the challenge through the fishing activity spots, then focus on clean technique: cast accurately, manage line tension, and do not rush the reel-in, because lost fish cost more time than slow ones. If Cal wins a round, the challenge can simply be tried again — nothing is locked by losing. Better bait or an upgraded rod, if the game offers them, makes his target score much easier to beat.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game at any arcade cabinet in Leonida. Walk up to a cabinet, pick the game, and play it through to its completion screen — a quick game over is not a completion, so pick the simplest title on offer if you just want the trophy. This also counts as one of the activity types for Master of None, so it does double duty. It takes only a few minutes and can be done the first time you pass an arcade.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete Andy's stranger strand all the way to his final mission. Strands unlock in steps: after each mission for Andy, some in-game time or story progress may need to pass before his next marker appears, so check the map periodically rather than waiting beside him. Finishing his last mission pops the trophy and also counts toward the eight completed strands needed for Strangers & Freaks. Keep his missions ticking over alongside the story and the finale arrives naturally.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's stranger strand through to his final mission. The strand's title hints at water, so do not be surprised if a boat is involved — bring standard supplies and let the missions teach you what they need. Each completed step may need some in-game time before the next marker for Kenton appears, which is normal for stranger strands. His finale also counts toward the eight strands required by Strangers & Freaks.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete Billy's stranger strand, ending with his final mission. Follow Billy's markers whenever they appear; strands advance in stages and sometimes pause until you progress elsewhere or let time pass in game. The trophy pops at the end of his last mission, and the strand counts toward the eight needed for Strangers & Freaks. If a marker seems missing, check both characters' maps and sleep or save to advance the clock.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete eight full stranger mission strands anywhere in Leonida. A strand only counts when its final mission is done, so half-finished chains do not move the counter — the five named finales in this list (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone) are five of your eight. Pick up every question-mark marker you pass, because strands unlock more strands and some only appear at certain story stages. Track the count in your stats, and prioritise finishing open strands over starting new ones.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's stranger strand through his final mission. Randy's chain revolves around moving goods, so expect driving and delivery-style objectives — a sturdy, reasonably fast vehicle makes the whole strand smoother. Let in-game time pass between steps if his next marker is slow to appear. Finishing his finale pops the trophy and adds one more completed strand toward Strangers & Freaks.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete Tyrone's stranger strand, finishing with his final mission. Work his markers in order whenever they show up, and remember that strand steps can be separated by in-game time or story progress. The trophy unlocks at the end of the finale, and Tyrone's strand is one of the eight completions counted by Strangers & Freaks. Keep a habit of clearing open strand markers before starting new story chapters and none of these will backlog.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot across Leonida — 18 spots in total. The spots sit in scenic, quiet places: beaches, hilltops and overlooks, and each one only asks you to arrive and use the prompt. Sweep them region by region alongside your other collectibles so the travel overlaps. Keep a checklist as you go, because the game gives little feedback about which specific spots remain.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal that Bret asks you to track down. Start from Bret's hunting activity or strand marker and follow its tracking steps — unique-animal hunts usually mean reading signs, moving quietly and taking one clean shot at the end. Bring a suitable hunting weapon and approach from cover if the game models detection. Completing Bret's hunt pops the trophy, and the attempt can be retried if the animal escapes.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete three full Collectible Card sets. Cards are hidden pickups across Leonida, grouped into themed sets, and a set only counts when every card in it is found — so pick the three shortest sets and finish them completely rather than spreading pickups thinly across all sets. Cards glint at close range and often sit in interiors, rooftops and odd corners. Work with a per-set checklist and sweep one neighbourhood at a time.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK action at 100 different locations across Leonida. Locations are distinct spots, so repeating the same place does not add to the count — travel is the whole job here. Pair this with exploration for The Goodtime State and the meditation spots, since all three reward the same region-by-region sweep. Keep a simple tally per region so the last few locations are easy to hunt down instead of becoming a state-wide guessing game.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 of the game's challenges — the short scored tasks tracked in the challenges menu, separate from missions and activities. Open the menu early, see which challenges your normal play is already advancing, and pin a few easy ones to finish deliberately. Challenges are repeatable content with no fail state, so this is a steady accumulation trophy rather than a skill wall. If you play varied content — races, combat, driving, exploration — most of the 50 complete almost by themselves.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, earn a four-star wanted level and then lose it completely. The reliable setup: commit crimes together in a fast car until four stars show, then break line of sight — tunnels, alleys, parking structures and a quick vehicle swap all help — and stay hidden until the stars drain. Your partner must be with you for the escape, so do not split up mid-chase. It is repeatable at any time, so if an attempt ends in a bust, just set it up again.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops back-to-back with your partner while keeping a wanted level the whole time. Plan the route first: pick three shops close together, park a fast getaway car facing the exit, and move directly from one robbery to the next without hiding long enough for the stars to clear — losing the wanted level resets the chain. Your partner must be present, so keep them in the car between shops. If the police pin you down, break line of sight briefly but re-offend quickly to keep the level alive until the third shop is done.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. A vehicle is discovered by getting in and driving it, so make a habit of stealing anything you have not driven before — parked cars count just as much as rare spawns. Different districts spawn different traffic: wealthy areas, industrial zones, airports and rural roads all have their own pools, so explore widely. This pairs perfectly with registering vehicles on the Scooter Bros app for On the Spot, so do both whenever you take something new.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down five enemies during a single activation of Combat Focus, the slow-motion aiming ability. Set it up deliberately: find a spot where five or more enemies cluster — a gang operation or a busy mission firefight — weaken nobody beforehand, then trigger Focus and work target to target with headshots. A high-capacity, accurate weapon makes the chain far easier than a shotgun spread. If you fall short, your Focus meter refills through normal combat, so attempts are unlimited.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: This trophy is flagged missable because its official description — making an unscheduled departure at VCIA, the airport — implies a specific one-time story moment rather than free-roam play, and that flag is an inference from the description text. The safe approach is to keep a manual save before airport-related story beats, and when a departure presents itself during the VCIA storyline, take the unscheduled option instead of the scripted one. Note that story missions can be replayed from the pause menu (per the cited guides), which is why no chapter trophy is flagged — but a choice inside a moment like this is exactly what replays may not rewind, so save first. If the moment passes, reload the save rather than hoping free roam offers it again.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The cryptic description points at Rhinos — the military tanks. In practice this means getting into or dealing with a Rhino tank when the game puts one in front of you, most naturally during the late-story military encounters or by raiding where armour is stationed. A tank is its own safest seat: once you are inside one, staying in it and surviving the heat is the whole idea behind the joke description. If a story moment offers a Rhino, take it for a ride rather than running past it. Free-roam attempts on military armour also work — just expect a heavy wanted response.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. Scout the store first: note the staff, the alarm points and the quietest entrance, then go in controlled — no gunfire, no sprinting past witnesses, and keep anyone present calm or restrained as the robbery mechanics allow. The moment an alarm or a detection marker triggers, the attempt is void, so leave and let things reset rather than forcing it. A clean, slow robbery with an unmarked getaway car parked close is far easier than a fast one.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape each time. Vault robberies are the heavy end of the robbery activities: bring full armour, your best weapons and a planned escape route with a vehicle change, because the police response is serious. Each vault only counts once you have escaped and lost the heat, so a bust at the door wastes the whole run. Spread the five across different banks, learn the vault routine on the first, and the rest become a repeatable loop that also feeds your money trophies.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape with the take. Armored trucks appear as roaming events and at set routes; you need serious firepower or explosives to crack one open, so prepare before engaging rather than improvising with a pistol. Block the truck, deal with its guards, breach the rear doors, grab the cash and leave immediately — the escape is part of the requirement. Have a fast car and a hiding route ready, because the wanted level arrives quickly.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — the map is divided into 52 areas, and each one registers when you physically travel through it. Most of the state uncovers itself during the story, strands and collectible sweeps, so leave this until late and then compare your map against the region list to find the gaps. The leftovers are usually small islands, swamp pockets and mountain corners that no mission visits. A boat and a plane or helicopter make the final cleanup quick, and this pairs naturally with the WAiNK locations and meditation spots.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang — there are nine gangs, and each one must be hit at least once. Operations are marked gang sites such as stash houses and fronts; robbing the same gang twice does not advance the count, so track which colours you have already hit. Expect armed resistance scaled to the gang, and bring an escape vehicle because these robberies draw attention. Work through the gangs territory by territory alongside your map exploration.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. This is one of the quiet moment trophies: head to the Ocean Beach area, find a beachfront bar or cocktail spot, and order a drink where the view prompt is offered. These scene trophies trigger at specific spots rather than anywhere on the sand, so walk the beachfront strip and watch for an interaction prompt at bars facing the water. It takes a minute, costs a little cash, and can be done at almost any point in free roam.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — meaning through the glass, in a car, the way the series has always done it. Visit a vehicle showroom, get into one of the display cars, and drive it straight out through the showroom windows instead of the door. Any showroom car works; pick one you also have not discovered yet and it will count toward Whip It Good at the same time. Expect a small wanted level for the stunt, so be ready to move once you are outside.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley. Head to that specific alley, start a game of bowling, and complete the follow-through action the game asks for during play — in practice, play the bowling activity there properly rather than quitting mid-frame. Bowling also counts as an activity type for Master of None, so this visit does double duty. If the prompt is tied to a particular throw or minigame beat, finish the full game and it will register along the way.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: This trophy is flagged missable because its official description — a partnership with mass appeal — implies a specific shared moment between the two protagonists that the story presents once, and the flag is an inference from that cryptic wording. Keep a manual save before major partnership story beats, and when a joint scene or joint activity with a crowd or audience presents itself, take part fully instead of skipping past it. Story missions can be replayed from the pause menu (per the cited guides), which is why no chapter trophy is flagged — but a one-time partnership moment is exactly the kind of thing to insure with a save. If you suspect the moment just passed, reload and replay that beat before moving on.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: This trophy is flagged missable because its official description — choices made, for better or worse — implies decisions that cannot be unmade once taken, and the flag is an inference from that wording; the trophy tracks a large count of choices (500 on the official tracker), so it is about committing to decisions across the whole game. The practical approach: never reload to undo a story or dialogue choice, answer prompts as they come, and keep one continuous playthrough as your choice record. Story missions can be replayed from the pause menu (per the cited guides), which is why no chapter trophy is flagged — but replays do not rewrite a choice history, so treat first decisions as final. If you play decisively throughout, the count fills long before the credits.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: This trophy is flagged missable because its official description — second time's the charm — implies failing once and succeeding on a specific retry, a sequence tied to a particular event rather than general play, and the flag is an inference from that wording. When a story or activity moment presents a clear fail-then-retry beat, do not reload to erase the failure: let the first attempt fail, then succeed on the immediate second attempt. Keep a manual save before distinctive one-off events so you can reconstruct the sequence if you blow through it successfully the first time. Story missions can be replayed from the pause menu (per the cited guides), which is why no chapter trophy is flagged — but a scripted second-chance moment is safest caught live, with a save in hand.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness something strange. This is the list's odd-encounter trophy: somewhere in Leonida there is a weird event — lights, a sighting, something unexplained — and you need to be there when it happens. Such events usually sit far from missions: deep swamp, open water at night, or remote corners of the map, and they reward the exploration you are already doing for The Goodtime State. If the sky or your radio starts behaving oddly in the middle of nowhere, stop and watch instead of driving on. It is a moment trophy, not a combat one, so no preparation beyond curiosity is needed.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by — striking a pedestrian or enemy with a melee weapon from a moving vehicle. Ride as a passenger or on a bike where melee drive-by attacks are available, equip a melee weapon, and swing as you pass a target at moderate speed: too slow and you just stop beside them, too fast and the swing whiffs. A crowded sidewalk gives you several chances per pass. It only needs to connect once, and it can be done at any point in free roam.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies — vaults, trucks and operations — and are worthless until a contact cleans them, so build the habit of fencing bills after every robbery spree instead of sitting on them. The counter tracks the laundered total, not your bank balance, so spending the clean money does not set you back. Paired with Maximum Withdrawal and Pest Control, this fills steadily; if you are short late-game, repeat vault robberies purely as a bill farm.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 in total across all shops. This counts cumulative spending — clothes, weapons, ammo, vehicle mods, food, services — so it fills naturally if you actually use the economy instead of hoarding cash. The fastest deliberate route is vehicle customisation and high-end clothing, which burn money in big chunks. Do not sell-and-rebuy the same items hoping to farm it; only purchases count. By the time the robbery trophies are done you will likely be most of the way there without trying.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties — eight garages across Leonida. Garages appear as purchasable property icons once you can afford property, and each one only needs to be bought once. This is a money trophy in disguise: the total price is steep, so it belongs late in the run after the robbery and laundering income is flowing. Buy them as your balance allows rather than saving for a single spree, since owned garages also give you useful vehicle storage for the discovery grind.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. When you enter a vehicle you want to keep track of, use the app registration option so the vehicle is logged to your account — ten registrations is all it takes. Combine this with Whip It Good: every time you steal something new for the discovery count, register it before you ditch it, and both trophies advance on the same cars. Registrations are permanent, so there is no way to lose progress once a vehicle is logged.
